biography.plain_text: Andrea Merloni was an Italian industrialist from the family behind Indesit. His wealth came through the family's appliance business, whose chairmanship he took over from his father, Vittorio. Born in Rome and trained in political science, he also chaired ISTAO, the Adriano Olivetti management school in Ancona, for four years.

confidence.reason: Corporate and institutional biographies establish formation and leadership; direct financial evidence supports the family wealth mechanism. ISTAO's own condolence confirms2011-2015 tenure.

long_biography.plain_text:
Andrea Merloni sought to revive Benelli by combining the Italian motorcycle maker's racing heritage with new engineering. He acquired the business in his twenties, recruited designers and engineers, and commissioned a new factory. Its Tornado superbike carried an unusual rear-mounted radiator and took the brand back into World Superbike racing. The venture struggled commercially and eventually passed to Qianjiang.

His interest in motorcycles also produced a publishing venture. With his twin brother Aristide, Merloni created Motonline, an internet portal for riders. A partnership with Editoriale Domus subsequently developed the project into Dueruote, which launched as a monthly magazine in 2005.

confidence.reason: Detailed specialist reporting establishes the engineering and commercial venture; Dueruote's own remembrance confirms its origins. Conflicting precise Benelli acquisition/sale dates are omitted.
